method: Static PE parsing, Capstone disassembly and Rizin analysis; no native Windows execution or C2 contact. Fresh atomscan and cleave facts were collected for every target before edits.
external_sources: All three supplied tria.ge URLs were inaccessible. Filename labels and ML verdicts were not used as behavioral proof.
changes: Expand VMware version-port query for DX/EDX and recovered section labels.
Require PStore enumeration/ReadItem ABI wrappers, not just factory/report strings, in the credential-acquisition objective.
Require EOF byte-transfer code and current-image lookup in the packed executable-joiner objective.
Retain independently verified injector, backup deletion, association-hijack and exfiltration traits.
limits: Memory-image damage prevents claiming that the first two specimens successfully install or run standalone. Surviving code establishes hostile purpose. Static paths are not observed successful execution.

evidence: CRT entry 0x402674 reaches mode dispatcher 0x401cb0; modes select installation, DLL injection and cleanup.
0x401260 opens HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL and writes its replacement at 0x40133e.
0x401150 creates a target process and writes a DLL pathname to VirtualAllocEx memory. Resolved kernel32!LoadLibraryA and the remote pathname are arguments to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401900 constructs an Active Setup GUID key, writes StubPath, reads and patches its own image, writes a copy and launches it.
0x401390 obtains its short module filename, reads COMSPEC and launches /c del with that filename.
The resource DLL retains Storm banners/configuration but most code is zero. Its strings do not establish a working DDoS payload.
This is a damaged memory-style PE retaining UPX sections/stub, populated code and mixed decoded/XOR strings. No assumption of successful stock UPX decompression is needed.
0x428653 XORs each byte with a supplied key. Key 2 recovers the form Content-Type, autorun filenames/directive, PStore DLL and EXE association key; key 5 recovers the HTTP POST format.
0x42a20c visits drive roots C through X, requires GetDriveType=2, copies its installed image into the root, sets attributes 6 and writes [autorun] and ShellExecute=autorun.exe.
0x428aad sends Run keys, Schedule ImagePath and an EXE open-command wrapper through registry writer 0x428a68. The latter invokes RegSetValueEx with the provided path/data.
0x42a4d4 resolves PStoreCreateInstance and iterates categories/subcategories/items. 0x42b46c/0x42b4a8/0x42b4e7/0x42b532 call COM slots 0x38/0x3c/0x44/0x54 with the corresponding ABI argument counts.

0x42a48e formats credential records into report buffer 0x401000. 0x42acc8 acquires and returns that buffer. The reporting loop calls it at 0x42b07b, encodes the returned value at 0x42b0bf, appends it to the psdata form parameter and calls transport 0x42964e at 0x42b13a.
0x42964e prepares a TCP port-80 connection, formats the POST including its supplied body at 0x42978a, and passes that same request buffer to the send thunk at 0x4297ba.

0x42843b loads VMware magic 0x564d5868, command 10 and DX=0x5658, executes IN and checks returned EBX. Startup calls this probe at 0x42b1b2. The old detection missed both the 16-bit DX form and UPX0 label.

eXPressor wraps a PE with original code still visible in .data. The preserved original import descriptors at RVA 0x32f4 can be parsed independently of the active packer import directory at RVA 0x8318.
Original IAT reconstruction binds 0x403024 to DeleteFileA, 0x4030ec to fgetc, 0x4030f0 to fputc, 0x4030f4 to fwrite, 0x4030f8 to rename, 0x4030fc to fopen and 0x40301c to GetModuleFileNameA.
The drive walker selects executable candidates and compares .BAK/.bak/.GHO/gho. Four backup comparisons converge on DeleteFileA at 0x401c80; executable candidates instead call 0x401340 at 0x401c99.

0x401340 obtains its own image path. It opens a temporary output in wb mode and its own image in rb mode, transfers bytes through fgetc/fputc until EOF at 0x4014ed..0x401509, then adds a header and the host data. A second complete byte-transfer loop survives at 0x40155f.
The replacement path deletes the original and renames the combined temporary output to the host pathname at 0x401748. Other branches preserve/recover joined host content.
The Zombie.exe working-copy path and Chinese host-recovery message corroborate the label; neither filename alone establishes infection. No ransom/encryption behavior was found.

control_results.method: Inert synthetic VMware PE controls and nonexecuted sample mutations; matched/nonmatched test-rules results are retained in scratch/review/batch2-controls.
